disease_label_per_paper: Post-traumatic orbital cellulitis and orbital abscess caused by Eikenella corrodens
presentation_summary: A 59-year-old man presented with 3 days of left eyelid redness, swelling, pain, and reduced visual acuity after terrazzo mixture splashed into the left eye.

He irrigated the eye immediately with water, then developed mild eyelid redness, swelling, and discomfort the next day; by the third morning symptoms were severe with difficulty opening the eye, copious discharge, and blurred vision.

Initial ocular exam showed visual acuity 20/25 right and 20/63 left, intraocular pressures 12.3 and 11.0 mm Hg, severe left eyelid edema and hyperemia, dust-like secretions, mixed conjunctival hyperemia, central corneal nebula about 3 x 4 mm with fluorescein negative staining, clear anterior chamber, round reactive pupil, and uneven lens opacity obscuring the fundus.
Left lacrimal irrigation showed reflux through the same puncta and a small amount of bean-curd-like secretions around the upper punctum; compression of lacrimal sac/canaliculi produced no secretions.
Left eyeball inward rotation was limited; right eye movement was normal.
Physical exam found white patches of varying sizes on face and hands, and the clinical diagnoses included left orbital cellulitis, cataracts, lacrimal duct obstruction, and vitiligo.

oral amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium for at least 6 weeks after discharge

clinical_course.description: Severe ocular pain, difficulty opening the left eye, and copious dust-like conjunctival secretions persisted; fever developed within 2 days, peaking at 38.8 C and resolving with ibuprofen.
Left eye pain with headache, persistent swelling, large purulent conjunctival secretions, unremarkable blood culture/cranial CT, orbit CT and MRI suggesting left orbital inflammation/injury.
A 2 x 3 mm medial upper eyelid palpebral conjunctival sinus tract discharged purulent material; irrigation and debridement reduced eyelid swelling.
Recurrent left eyelid edema and headache led to antibiotic escalation and ultrasound-guided aspiration of a 23 x 13 x 13 mm orbital collection.
Clinical improvement with only minimal purulent discharge remaining.
Recurrent eyelid swelling and increased bloody-purulent discharge suggested abscess reformation, requiring sinus tract debridement and drainage strip.
After drainage strip removal, minimal bloody and purulent discharge remained from a sinus tract about 1.5 cm long.

outcome_follow_up.description: No eye pain or headache; swelling nearly subsided; left visual acuity improved to 20/50 with intraocular pressure 10 mmHg and normal eye movements.

outcome_follow_up.source_text_value: left eye visual acuity 20/50 before discharge

outcome_follow_up.description: Discharged on oral amoxicillin-clavulanate potassium for at least 6 weeks with weekly ophthalmology follow-up.

quality_warnings: Eikenella culture, orbital abscess aspiration, later imaging, antibiotic switches, debridement, drainage strip, and treatment response are use_in_ranking:false.
Initial post-traumatic presentation, reduced acuity, eyelid edema/hyperemia, discharge, and limited inward rotation are preserved as ranking evidence.
CRP and hypokalemia are early hospital data but not presentation-time evidence here, so they are saved outside ranking observations.
